facts.statement: The holotype fossil of Triunfosaurus was discovered in sandstone layers of the Rio Piranhas Formation in the state of Paraíba, Brazil.
facts.quote: The holotype of Triunfosaurus, UFRJ-DG 498, was found in a sandstone layer of the Rio Piranhas Formation to the west of Paraíba State, Brazil.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton containing three tail vertebrae, three chevrons, three neural spines, and a right ischium.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton including a series of three middle tail vertebrae (subsequently considered to be vertebrae from the front of the tail), three isolated chevrons, three isolated neural spines, and a right ischium.

facts.statement: Triunfosaurus leonardii was named and described in 2017 by a team of six researchers led by Ismar de Souza Carvalho.
facts.quote: The type and only species Triunfosaurus leonardii was named and described in 2017 by Ismar de Souza Carvalho, Leonardo Salgado, Rafael Matos Lindoso, Hermínio Ismael de Araújo-Júnior, Francisco Cézar Costa Nogueira and José Agnelo Soares.

facts.statement: The Rio Piranhas Formation, where Triunfosaurus fossils were found, is dated to the Berriasian to Valanginian stages, possibly extending into the Hauterivian.
facts.quote: Based on correlation using pollen and co-occurrence of similar trackways, the Rio Piranhas Formation has been considered as a contemporary of the Sousa Formation, which extends from the Berriasian to the Valanginian, and possibly into the Hauterivian (correlating to the Rio da Serra and early Aratu faunal stages).

facts.statement: Triunfosaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 145 to 130 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 145 a 130 millones de años, desde el Berriasiense al Hauteriviense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Vertebrae near the front of the tail possess short, robust prezygapophyses that are slightly angled upwards from the horizontal.
facts.quote: The vertebrae from near the front of the tail have short and robust processes, or prezygapophyses, on their front edges; these processes are also slightly angled upwards from the horizontal.

facts.statement: The rear sides of the vertebral centra are strongly concave, while the pleurocoels (depressions on the sides) are relatively small.
facts.quote: The back half of the sides of the centra are strongly concave, while the depressions on the sides of the vertebrae known as pleurocoels are rather small.

facts.statement: The internal texture of the vertebrae is not sponge-like or camellate.
facts.quote: The internal textures of the centra are not sponge-like, or camellate.

facts.statement: More than 535 individual dinosaur trackways have been found in the Triunfo Basin.
facts.quote: The Triunfo Basin is better known for presence of ichnotaxa; more than 535 individual trackways produced by dinosaurs are known from the basin.

facts.statement: Some of the dinosaur footprints found in the basin may have been made by Triunfosaurus.
facts.quote: Some of these footprints may have been made by Triunfosaurus.

facts.statement: The environment where Triunfosaurus lived likely consisted of alluvial fans and river systems.
facts.quote: The environment probably consisted of alluvial fans and systems of rivers.

facts.statement: Triunfosaurus was initially classified as a basal titanosaur but was later reassigned to the Somphospondyli due to conflicting evidence.
facts.quote: It was initially described as a basal titanosaur, making it the earliest basal titanosaur known; however, subsequent research questioned the identification of the taxon as a titanosaur, instead reassigning it to the Somphospondyli.

facts.statement: Researchers argue that the feature used to classify Triunfosaurus as a titanosaur is also found in non-titanosaur somphospondylans like Phuwiangosaurus and Tangvayosaurus.
facts.quote: Poropat et al. noted that the furrow separating the arch into two surfaces, used by Carvalho et al. to assign Triunfosaurus to the Titanosauria, is likewise present in the non-titanosaur somphospondylans Phuwiangosaurus and Tangvayosaurus.

facts.statement: The assignment of certain tail vertebrae to the middle of the tail is questioned by some researchers.
facts.quote: Additionally, the assignment of the caudal vertebrae to the middle of the tail was also questioned by Poropat et al..

facts.statement: Due to the problematic nature of the fossil evidence, some researchers have reassigned Triunfosaurus to the Somphospondyli rather than Titanosauria.
facts.quote: For these reasons, Poropat et al. reassigned Triunfosaurus to the Somphospondyli, being unable to confidently support its titanosaurian affinities due to its problematic nature.

facts.statement: While Triunfosaurus was initially used to support a Gondwanan origin for titanosaurs, an alternate hypothesis suggesting dispersal from Europe remains plausible.
facts.quote: Nevertheless, an alternate hypothesis involving dispersal out of Europe remains plausible.

facts.statement: Triunfosaurus was a medium-sized sauropod.
facts.quote: Triunfosaurus era un saurópodo de tamaño mediano.

facts.statement: The ischium of Triunfosaurus has a unique shape where the pubic contact area is half the total height and the shaft angles less than 70 degrees relative to the femoral articulation.
facts.quote: Una es que la parte del isquion en contacto con el hueso púbico tiene la mitad de la altura del isquion entero, y el eje del isquion tiene un ángulo de menos de 70° con respecto a la parte que forma la articulación con el fémur, el acetábulo.

facts.statement: Triunfosaurus is distinguished from all other titanosaurs by the unique proportions of its ischium.
facts.quote: Como género, Triunfosaurus se puede distinguir de todos los demás titanosaurianos por las proporciones únicas de su isquión.

facts.statement: The neural spines on Triunfosaurus vertebrae are small and feature midline processes that expand near the top.
facts.quote: En la parte superior de las vértebras, las espinas neurales son pequeñas y tienen procesos a lo largo de sus líneas medias que se expanden cerca de la parte superior.

facts.statement: Two small crests at the base of the posterior hemal arch form a crest-like structure.
facts.quote: En la base del arco en la parte posterior, dos pequeñas crestas forman una estructura en forma de cresta.

facts.statement: The holotype of Triunfosaurus was found in the Rio Piranhas Formation in Brazil, dating from the Berriasian to Hauterivian, approximately 145 to 130 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Triunfosaurus, UFRJ-DG 498, fue hallado en una capa de arenisca en la Formación Rio Piranhas en Brasil, la cual data de la épocas del Berriasiense al Hauteriviense, hace cerca de 145 a 130 millones de años.

facts.statement: Triunfosaurus leonardii was named and described in 2017 by Ismar de Souza Carvalho, Leonardo Salgado, Rafael Matos Lindoso, Hermínio Ismael de Araújo-Júnior, Francisco Cézar Costa Nogueira, and José Agnelo Soares.
facts.quote: La especie tipo y única conocida, Triunfosaurus leonardii fue nombrada y descrita en 2017 por Ismar de Souza Carvalho, Leonardo Salgado, Rafael Matos Lindoso, Hermínio Ismael de Araújo-Júnior, Francisco Cézar Costa Nogueira y José Agnelo Soares.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the Triunfo Basin in Paraíba combined with the Greek suffix for 'lizard', while the species name honors paleontologist Giuseppe Leonardi.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se refiere a la Cuenca Triunfo en Paraíba, combinado con el sufijo griego sauros, "lagarto", mientras que el nombre de la especie es en honor del paleontólogo Giuseppe Leonardi.

facts.statement: Poropat et al. reassigned Triunfosaurus to Somphospondyli, unable to confidently support its affinities with titanosaurs due to its problematic nature.
facts.quote: Poropat et al. Triunfosaurio reasignadolo a Somphospondyli, siendo incapaz de apoyar con confianza sus afinidades con los titanosaurianos debido a su naturaleza problemática.

facts.statement: The parent group of Triunfosaurus is Somphospondyli.
facts.quote: Parent group: Somphospondyli

facts.statement: Triunfosaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Triunfosaurus lived during the Berriasian to Hauterivian, from 143.1 to 125.77 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Hauterivian (143.1 to 125.77 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is considered probable that the maker of the sauropod tracks found in the Triunfo Basin was Triunfosaurus itself.
facts.quote: Se considera probable que el realizador de esas huellas fuera el propio Triunfosaurus.

facts.statement: The environment likely consisted of alluvial deltas and river systems.
facts.quote: El ambiente probablemente consistía en deltas aluviales y sistemas de ríos.

facts.statement: Vertebrae near the front of the tail have short, robust prezygapophyses on their front edges that are slightly inclined upward from the horizontal.
facts.quote: Las vértebras cerca de la parte delantera de la cola tienen procesos cortos y robustos, o prezigapófisis, en sus bordes delanteros; estos procesos también están ligeramente inclinados hacia arriba desde la horizontal.

facts.statement: In the hemal arches of the lower vertebrae near the front of the tail, the hemal canals are narrow and the arches themselves are relatively straight.
facts.quote: En los arcos hemales de la parte inferior de las vértebras cerca de la parte delantera de la cola, los agujeros que forman con el centro, los canales hemales, son estrechos y los arcos mismos son relativamente rectos.

facts.statement: An alternative hypothesis involving dispersal from Europe remains plausible.
facts.quote: Una hipótesis alternativa que involucra la dispersión fuera de Europa sigue siendo plausible.

facts.statement: A 2026 redescription by Mannion & Carvalho interprets Triunfosaurus leonardii as a member of Somphospondyli belonging to or closely related to Titanosauria.
facts.quote: Redescription of the anatomy and a study on the affinities of Triunfosaurus leonardii is published by Mannion & Carvalho (2026), who interpret the studied species as a member of Somphospondyli belonging or closely related to Titanosauria.
